newsitem.title: USA: American Medical to acquire STAT Healthcare.
newsitem.headline: American Medical to acquire STAT Healthcare.

text.p: American Medical Response Inc., a major ambulance service provider, will acquire STAT Healthcare Inc., an emergency health services company, in a deal valued at about $145 million, the companies said Tuesday.

Under the definitive agreement, American Medical will offer 0.25 share of its stock for each STAT common share in a tax-free pooling of interests. American Medical will issue about 4 million shares based upon the exchange ratio, it said.
STAT's stock rose 62.5 cents to $9 on Nasdaq at mid-morning. American Medical fell 50 cents to $37 on the New York Stock Exchange.

"The acquisition of STAT adds a range of complementary health care services to our core business as the nation's leading ambulance service provider," said Paul T. Shirley, chief executive officer of American Medical.

"This is consistent with our strategy, which began with our development of American Medical Pathways, of transforming from an emergency and non-emergency transportation company to a health care company providing a broader spectrum of services."
STAT's services are expected to generate about $35 million in revenue in 1996 for the merged company, up 51 percent from over 1995, they said.

Houston-based STAT provides contract management services to affiliated physician groups that staff the emergency departments of 24 hospitals, mainly in southeast Texas. STAT contracts with over 200 physicians and provides emergency services to more than 300,000 patients annually.

American Medical provides emergency and non-emergency ambulance services in 28 states. The Aurora, Colo.-based company said it plans to continue acquiring ambulance providers and complementary health care providers.
STAT stockholders holding about 60 percent of the company's shares have agreed to vote in favour of the merger, which is expected to close by year-end, the companies said.
